maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Apparently we are to acquire another eleven destroyers; is it not possible to have some of them built in Canada?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes, it would be possible to build in this country but the expense would be high.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Half as much again.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: We have had estimates made. It would cost more.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Approximately what is the difference in cost?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
The
estimates vary because of wage schedules, et cetera, indicating a difference of perhaps from 15 to 40, or more, per cent. My recollection of the last figures I got is a cost of between five and six millions in Canada for two.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What was it in England?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
What does that five millions
represent?

Supply-National Defence

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: The cost of two destroyers built in Canada.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Of one destroyer?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Two.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
What do they cost in
England?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
I am
not sure, but they are not as costly in England. I believe the last and the most modern that has been built in the United States cost about 86,000,000. The last two we purchased for our own purposes cost about $3,375,000.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: The other day the minister said that plans were to be drawn up during the coming year for the construction in Canada of anti-submarine vessels and motor torpedo boats. Is there any vote in this year's estimates for the actual construction of those smaller craft?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
The Naval Service Act,
at section 45, reads as follows:
The Naval Discipline Act 1866, and the acts in amendment thereof passed by the parliament of the United Kingdom for the time being in force, and the King's regulations and Admiralty instructions, in so far as the said acts, regulations and instructions are applicable, and except in so far as they may be inconsistent with this act or with any regulations made under this act, shall apply to the naval service and shall have the same force in law as if they formed part of this act.
Section 46 states:
The Naval Discipline (Dominion Naval Forces) Act, 1911, enacted by the parliament of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland shall apply to the naval forces raised by the Dominion of Canada and the ships provided for such naval forces, subject to the modifications, adaptations and exceptions set out in the last preceding section.
There is an order of the house asking for a copy of The Naval Discipline Act 1866, and amendments thereto, and for the Naval Discipline (Dominion Naval Forces) Act, 1911. I have not been able to secure copies of these acts from the usual sources, and I now ask the minister if it is possible to table in the house the copies I should like to have, inasmuch as they apply in very important respects to our naval forces.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes, certainly.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: When will they be tabled?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Probably the next sitting day.

Item agreed to.
Naval services.
191.	Naval stores chargeable to ordinary account, $1,451,772.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Are we depending on Great Britain for naval stores, such as guns, antisubmarine equipment, and so on?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
For the
procurement of them?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
We cannot manufacture
any of those supplies in Canada?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: No. The guns are imported from Great Britain.

Item agreed to.
Naval services.
192.	Naval stores chargeable to capital account, $930,900.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What is meant by the expressions "chargeable to ordinary account" and "chargeable to capital account"?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I explained that fully the other day; perhaps the hon. member was not here. It was also explained by the Minister of Finance on a former occasion this session. But if my hon. friend w'ishes, I shall explain it again.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: No; I shall refer to Hansard.

Item agreed to.
Naval services.
198. Naval engineering, chargeable to ordinary account, $993,365.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What is the present strength of the reserves?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Does the hon. member mean the present strength of the Royal Canadian Naval Reserves?

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I would point out that we are discussing item 193, not 195.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: There has been some suggestion that Coal Harbour in Vancouver should be dredged by the dominion government with the idea of using it as a base for small naval boats. Can the minister tell us whether or not that work is to be done, and if so if that is the objective?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
I think the work is being done as a general harbour improvement. But incidentally the completion of that work would no doubt provide a
Supply-National Defence

useful point from which small power boats could put to sea rapidly, when attending to the inlets on the British Columbia coast.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Has the government looked into the possibility of using Turner Valley oil for Canadian naval ships on the Pacific coast and also for British naval ships putting in at our ports?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes, the matter has been carefully considered.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What is the possibility of using that oil?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Nothing has been definitely settled yet in regard to it. Substantial difficulties have been encountered in connection with practical results. I understand, unofficially, that a representative of the admiralty has been in touch with the situation there.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Are any negotiations
proceeding between the federal government and the British government in regard to Turner valley oil?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Not as far as I know.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Is the minister aware of any negotiations by any other government?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Many
letters have been received by departmental representatives in connection with the point raised by the hon. member for Vancouver South, outlining the possibility and the practicability of running a pipe line from the Turner Valley either to the Pacific coast at Vancouver, or to Fort William. I understand, unofficially, that various people interested in the situation have been making investigations. But no federal government action has been taken.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Does the government consider an investigation necessary in connection with laying a pipe line?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Our
requirements of oil are comparatively small, in view of the limited- number of Canadian naval vessels. But the requirements of the British Admiralty would be a different matter altogether.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
I understand that
Esquimalt is also a base for British ships. Has there been any investigation by the British government into the necessity of establishing a pipe line to the Turner Valley oil fields?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
So far as my memory goes, I do not think any

investigation has been made through our department. It is possible, however, that it may have been made directly, through their representative.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: And there is no representative from the minister's department in England at the present time?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Not on that point, so far as I know.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I understand that under the contractual agreement between the British and dominion governments with respect to the bases at Esquimalt and Halifax, the Canadian government has become responsible for the stores and fuel supplies.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes, it has been for a long time.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I notice that the refueling of some of his majesty's ships was undertaken by a tanker ship sent across the Atlantic, in connection with the royal visit. Have we developed facilities for refueling at these bases?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: The hon. member will notice in the supplementary estimates there is an item of $300,000 to look after the fueling of Canadian naval ships, for the construction of tanks on Vancouver island.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Does that include ships of his majesty's navy?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
The
Canadian navy.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: And the royal navy, too.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
I am
afraid the storage capacity of tanks provided would not be sufficient for all purposes.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Would these ships be oil burners?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: The destroyers are oil burners.

Item agreed to.
Naval services.
195. Royal Canadian naval reserves, $429,099.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: The minister said the other day that some sort of schooner was to be provided on the Pacific coast for the training of naval recruits.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Would the minister give us details of the methods used at the present time in the training of those recruits? There have been requests for a training ship at

Supply-National Defence
Vancouver similar to those used in Great Britain, but as yet, no move has been made in that direction.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: There are several methods pursued by various branches of the naval reserves. As a matter of fact some of the best branches of the naval volunteer reserves in Canada are stationed in prairie cities. They are very efficient, and go for training to the Pacific coast. Training takes place on the Atlantic coast, where they go to the West Indies under sail. They take training in steamship, under naval seamen, and in duties incidental to proper naval training. Of course there is shore training as well. At Esquimalt there are stations which carry out a thorough shore training for the benefit of recruits.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What is the present strength of the reserves?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Royal
Canadian Naval Reserve is made up of 67 officers and 197 ratings. The Royal Canadian Naval Volunteer Reserve is made up of 124 officers and 1,396 other ranks. That was the strength in March, 1939.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Would those figures
include members of the fishermen's reserve?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Their
strength was 200.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Is there to be any addition to this reserve?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: We are providing in the estimates this year for a total strength of 400. It is intended to have the same force on the Atlantic as on the Pacific.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I should like to revert to item 194 for a moment, and inquire as to where the fuel oil used by the Canadian navy is obtained.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: From the commercial oil companies. In some cases the storage is only commercial oil, but the naval people prefer to have what is known as naval fuel oil. I understand the Turner Valley oil produces a high grade of gasoline.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Are any of the supplies now being used imported from abroad, and if so from where?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I believe most of the oil is imported, but I have not the figures before me.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Could we have the quantities used?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I have the figures in my office, but not here.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Will the minister kindly send them to me?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I asked that question on a previous occasion and I was told supplies were obtained in most cases from the Imperial Oil Company, the oil possibly coming from the United States.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Is there any system of promotion in the navy whereby a man could pass all the way up the ladder through the various ranks, or are there barriers in the way?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: No. As a matter of fact quite a number are promoted to commissioned rank.	v

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I understand when these boys go on leave they have to pay their railroad fares to their homes.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Naval
personnel travelling on duty are allowed special rates over the Canadian railway lines of two and a half cents per mile for first-class passage, and one and two-third cents a mile for second-class passage. This special rate applies in all cases where naval personnel are travelling on duty, and also where ratings are travelling on leave, in which case the department assumes any part of the cost. Where naval personnel are travelling on private business no part of the cost is paid by the department, and they are not entitled to this special rate.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I cannot understand why these men should have to pay their fares back home when they go on leave.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: One-half the cost of transportation is recovered from ratings going on leave. A rating may be granted second-class transportation at the public expense to his home and return, but one-half the cost of such transportation is recovered.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Are the men in the fishermen's reserve being trained, and are the boats being equipped in any way for an emergency?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
They
were gathered together at a central point in British Columbia for a period of one month. They did a certain amount of shore training, a certain amount of signalling, and went to sea on several occasions to practise formation work. They were trained generally in naval duties which would be necessary for the protection of the coast. I believe this work has been successful in every way.
Supply-National Defence

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Do they receive any training in mine laying?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Most
definitely.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Will the vessels be equipped with guns?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I imagine they will carry light guns, or rather machine guns.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Would the minister consider allowing these men all their fares?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I shall be glad to take up that matter.

Item agreed to.
Air services.
196. Royal Canadian Air Force-permanent active air force, $3,992,686.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I understand there are twelve aeroplane manufacturing plants in Canada, six of which assemble aero-engines. Have these twelve plants been given every opportunity to supply the requirements of the department in connection with new planes?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I would say so.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I understand that under this item provision is made for the building of air fields in various parts of Canada. Could some consideration be given to helping in the development of air fields now being used by air lines not government owned? I have in mind the airport at Peace River, which is used by commercial planes and by planes transporting mail as far north as the Yukon and Alaska. Considerable work could be done in connection with the development of this airport. There is a good deal of commercial flying out of Peace River, and a small expenditure would prove most useful in time of need. I am sure the minister realizes that this is one of the main links in a line of communication that would be absolutely necessary in time of emergency.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I shall be glad to consider the representations of my hon. friend.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
On an earlier item the minister was good enough to answer my question referring to the aircraft manufacturers in Canada. I think he will realize that the successful and economical manufacture of aircraft is dependent upon continuous production. Many of these companies have trained a staff of most efficient operators, but at the moment orders are coming in spasmodically. The result is they

have their flat periods when it is difficult to find work for the men. Many men leave the plants, and when new orders come in, their services are not available for production. Has the minister any plan of providing continuous production in these plants?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
That
matter is definitely before the department.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: A good work is being done in many of the technical schools in providing training which proves highly useful when a lad enters the air force later on. Some of the universities in other countries have most extensive aeronautical courses. Students who graduate from these courses as engineers find their progress much more rapid when they join the air force later. Has the minister any information to give as to what work is going forward at the moment?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
We are
taking on quite a number of mechanics this year, as my hon. friend may have noticed. I shall be glad to give the other matter he mentions full, consideration.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Has the government taken any active interest in helping in the development of courses at the school of science in connection with the university of Toronto, and other engineering schools throughout the country.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What centres in the eastern provinces will be used for the training of pilots for the permanent air force?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: There are eight flying clubs where ab initio training will be carried out, and these clubs cooperate with the department under the new scheme. They are located at Vancouver, Calgary, Regina, Winnipeg, Toronto, Hamilton, Montreal and Halifax.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: There will be no training at the air fields at Yarmouth, Truro and Sydney? This training will be carried on only at Dartmouth?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: At Halifax, under this scheme of flying clubs cooperation.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What will be the activities of the air force at the port of St. John? Will any pilots be trained there?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
The chief of the air staff surveyed the situation in St. John a week ago, and he will be making a complete report on the requirements. As my hon. friend knows, a non-permanent squadron is stationed there.

Supply-National Defence

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: How many pilots are now being trained at Trenton?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Between 60 and 70 under the old scheme. More will be trained there under the new scheme.
Mr, MASSEY: Where will the fifty British pilots be trained?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: They will take their ab initio training in Great Britain. Some of our Canadian pilots will take their ab initio training in the flying clubs. The intermediate training will be at Camp Borden, which will be substantially reconditioned and reconstructed for the purpose. The third period of training, the advanced stage, will be taken at Trenton. A total of 126 will be trained under the scheme. Much of this year's vote will have to go into equipment and buildings to provide the facilities required for at least two stages of training. Probably next year, with a similar vote, the number of pilots in training will be substantially increased.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Will there be any training at Regina?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
The
personnel will be divided among the eight flying clubs that I mentioned.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
What is the policy pursued by the minister and the department in respect of the $4,000,000 for the permanent air force? Will the practice in the old country be followed of seeking the aid of school boards, cities and towns, to recruit for the air force?
Some of the graduating high school population might join. I appreciate the activity of the minister and his department, but I think we could obtain a large number of splendid recruits for the permanent and nonpermanent air force by following such a long term policy as they have in Great Britain, Mr. Brown, Minister of Labour there, Mr. Belisha, Secretary for War, with the Air Minister and other ministers, were in the city of York, England, not long ago, addressing the board of education and city council at a banquet in the town hall, where they laid down a long term policy for recruiting the youth of the old country for the permanent and non-permanent air force. Great Britain was behind in building up its air force, but is now catching up. They have a long term policy for the air force extending up to five or seven years, during which period the recruit receives board, clothing, lodging and some pocket money; I think there is also deferred pay, $1.10 a day in the second year. In training for the permanent air force they can also learn a trade as an apprentice, so
that at the end of the training period they are fitted for a position as pilot or air mechanic or in other key industries.
What is the policy of this government for the air force? Have they any such policy as would be adapted to Canada's circumstances? I believe that a very large body of our unemployed youth would make desirable recruits for the air force. We have four thousand miles of country with practically no protection for the civilian population from attacks from the air. I know that we are starting to arm, but it will be years and years before our civilian population will have adequate air protection of any kind whatever. Not only would many of our unemployed youth make desirable recruits for the air force, but it would give them an opportunity to learn a useful calling and take them off relief. Do not forget what Canada did in the great war. Toronto district alone, in the war trained 18,000 mechanics and pilots for the Royal Air Force, and some of the most brilliant air pilots were Canadians. We should have a long-range policy of air defence, which would also help to take care of our unemployed youth in addition to a defence policy. Will the minister tell us what is proposed to be done on such a long-range policy for Canada and the mother country as well.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
The
training of mechanics will be done in a substantial way as part of the youth training scheme. As I explained when presenting my estimates, provision is made for the first time in the estimates this year for short service commissions in the Canadian air force, following a similar practice adopted in England some years ago of serving four years in the active air force and then a number of years on the reserve.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Is it proposed to have
any national register of the man power available for the permanent air force or defence purposes? Has any survey been made of possible recruits or a defence register before it is too late?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
No
definite survey has yet been made.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Are recruits still being accepted in Canada for the Royal Air Force? The practice has been, as I understand it, to accept young men tentatively in various parts of Canada for the Royal Air Force, and then bring them to Ottawa for a final medical examination. The medical examination here is very strict; I have known young men who have been accepted in other parts
Supply-National Defence

of the country rejected on medical examination here. I am thinking of a case particularly from Saskatoon, which I brought to the attention of the minister last year. This young man was turned down when he got here, and I have heard of several such cases Could not some arrangement be made to prevent the hardship of being tentatively accepted in other parts of the country and finally turned down here and left more or less stranded?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: My hon. friend is quite correct. In the old days Canadians who wished to join the Royal Air Force had to go to England and run the risk of being rejected there and sent back home. Under the present system a man may be rejected upon medical examination in Ottawa, but now that we have western, eastern and central air commands, I see no reason why they could not be medically examined with finality before coming to Ottawa.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Will the minister see
if that can be arranged?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I shall be glad to look into the matter.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: A moment ago I asked a question with regard to candidates for the Royal Air Force from technical schools. A few months ago application was made to the Minister of Labour by the board of education of the city of Toronto in connection with the aeronautics course which the central technical school is giving. The difficulty they experience is that they have no adequate equipment, and no building in which to operate, but such work as they have been doing has been done exceedingly well, and those trained in the course have been eminently successful in finding positions. Would it be possible for the Minister of National Defence, as the Minister of Labour states he is unable to take care of the matter, to give consideration to the possibility of extending assistance to the technical school in Toronto to provide training along this line?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What are the educational requirements for admission to the Canadian Air Force?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
It depends entirely on the category in which they wish to enlist. There are five or six and more different categories:	enlistment of
unskilled men, enlistment of skilled men, enlistment of air men for training as tradesmen. As regards the last:
In addition to the general qualifications outlined in paragraph 6-

Which I will read later.
-an applicant for enlistment in the R.C.A.F. for training as a tradesman must:-
(a)	Have attained his 18th but not his 25th birthday on the first of June of the year in which his training commences.
(b)	Be a graduate of a recognized technical school and have specialized in a trade allied to an air force trade, or
(c)	Be in possession of a junior matriculation certificate or its equivalent.
13. Airmen entering the air force under the requirements of this section are given instruction in a recognized air force trade. This instruction lasts for approximately one year, and if the airman successfully completes it, he is employed in the trade for which he appears to be best suited, and will be remustered as a tradesman as soon as he passes the necessary trade test, provided that there is a vacancy in his particular trade.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What are the requirements for aircraftsmen?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
The
same.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I ask that these qualifications be put on Hansard so that we may have the information.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: With the permission of the committee, if there is no objection, I shall be very glad to table the regulations.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Agreed.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
I believe the minister,
speaking the other day, mentioned that there are fifty British airmen training in Canada. Is that correct? Are these British airmen training under our officers and with our facilities?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: There will be altogether, I believe, from Great Britain, 12 or 14 instructors as well as our own. Of course, the personnel required for training purposes is very substantial indeed, and a large amount of the costs entailed is for the ground personnel and the various types of training personnel required. Special instructors will come over for that purpose.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
It would seem to me, in view of the limited facilities we have for training Canadians who enlist in the air force, and our lack of facilities generally, that it would have been well had our department allowed the British authorities to send over instructors to train airmen in Canada. I understand also that had the original idea been carried out and the British not been limited to training under Canadian facilities, far more British airmen would be training in Canada. Is that correct, and was it the original intention to train British airmen in Canada on a more extended scale than is proposed at the present time?

Supply-National Defence

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I believe that when the scheme was first suggested, that statement would be correct. But after they sent an officer over here to survey the situation in Canada the first proposals were substantially modified. They are satisfied with the arrangements now, and have expressed their appreciation of the cooperation they have received.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Was it the political "situation " that the minister referred to, or the training facilities of the Canadian air force, which limited the action of the British authorities?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I do not know anything at all about the first part of the question.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What was the reason for the change from the original proposal to have British air force instructors come to Canada and assist in the training for one, two or three years, as they did in the great war? During the last war a great many trained British air force men, and men of the British munitions board, came over here as instructors and pilots and trained for the Royal Air Force. Some of them stayed in Canada. Some of their greatest pilots came over to assist us, and we were dependent upon Britain for the training of Canadians in Canada in ten or twelve camps. I fail to see what good reason there is for the change in such a splendid policy. I have been reading about it and have been looking into the reports, and I can see no necessity for the change; quite the reverse, for very few of the Canadian pilots who served in the war are available for this work, and the restriction is not in accordance with good public policy. It would be far better if we had the benefit of the advice of capable men from the British air force. What is the reason for this change, and who recommended it?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Following the discussion we had in this house last year, the British government sent an expert over here; he surveyed the situation and went back to Great Britain with all the data he could possibly obtain, and made a report to the government. It is as a result of the report he made that we have the scheme which we have to-day. I assure my hon. friend that there has been nothing but full cooperation between the Department of National Defence and the British air ministry with reference to this whole matter, and we have letters on our file to prove their appreciation of our cooperation.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What was the original number the British authorities requested should be trained over here?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I do not recall the exact number; I doubt if any definite number was proposed. There were numbers suggested from time to time, but my recollection now is, and I am speaking subject to correction, that we offered to train more than the number which eventually they asked us to train.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Can the minister say when the original request was made, and from whom it came? Did we suggest that we were prepared to train British pilots, or did the request come from the United Kingdom?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: My hon. friend will recall that we had a discussion about this in the house last year.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Quite so.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I believe a statement was made in this house, and also in the British parliament.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: But at that time the minister stated that if a request were made by the British government, it would not be refused. He said no request had then been made. Subsequently, after prorogation, the question arose again. Did we make the suggestion to the United Kingdom, or did they make it to us?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I would not be certain about that. I shall have to look up the record, but my present belief is that we made the suggestion. However, we must be positive of our facts.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I gather from what the minister said this afternoon that the fifty who are to be trained now are merely a beginning. We hope that we may be able to do more in the future; this is essentially a trial-is that it?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
That
entirely depends on the future. What I did say was that if the government recommends to parliament next year a vote similar to the item of 86,000,000 for the training of pilots, we shall then have done so much by getting equipment, intermediate trainers, and advanced trainers, and reconditioning the buildings and the grounds which must be reconditioned, that there will be more money available for training personnel.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Camp Borden is now to be made an all-year field?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Can the change to which I have referred be said to have had the effect of showing lack of coordination and cooperation with the air force of the mother country?
Supply-National Defence

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: It shows the very opposite, because we have a definite expression of appreciation from the air ministry of the cooperation they have received.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Is this a training plan for a period of three years?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I understood the minister to say the other day that there would not be more than fifty British pilots trained here in any one of these three years?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: So that the total number of British pilots who can be trained under the scheme will be 150?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Not necessarily, because the number could be modified from year to year. But the understanding between the two governments is for the period of three years. As to the actual numbers, it says only a minimum of fifty: that could be quite easily changed by amending the agreement next year.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
The minister said that the
number of pilots coming from the United Kingdom for training would not exceed fifty in any one year.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: That is the agreement now. It can be changed at any time.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Will these men be under
the disciplinary control of the Canadian defence department?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: They will be under the direction of the Department of National Defence.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
I did not get a definite
answer to my question about manufacturing in Canada. It was not necessary for the minister to rely on his investigation with regard to the twelve manufacturing firms, because to my own knowledge they have been in pretty close touch with the department. Can the minister elaborate on the quantity of work he has been able to give to these manufacturing firms? It would appear that there is an opportunity to employ a largely increased number of men if these people can get orders.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
I quite
agree with my hon. friend that if we were not confronted with what appeared to be emergent conditions we could give them far more work than we have done in recent months; and I think any long-range policy

should be in the direction of encouraging industrial production in Canada as much as possible. In addition to the orders we were able to place with seven or eight firms, the department were largely responsible for negotiations with the British air mission, and the industry in Canada has been grateful, I believe, for the cooperation it received from the department. I appreciate the position taken by my hon. friend, and we shall be glad to cooperate.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Does the minister know
to what extent the British authorities have placed orders?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
I do
not know exactly.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: How many young men have been recruited in Canada for the royal air force in the last three years?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
For
some years we have been sending fifteen to England, but last year, under the policy announced in 1937, there were 120, so that to-day there are three schemes-15, 120 and the third scheme I have referred to.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
How many
were recruited for the Canadian air force last year?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: In January, 1937, the strength of the Royal Canadian Air Force was 152 officers and 958 other ranks, or 1,110; and in April, 1939, it was .261 officers and 1,951 other ranks, or 2,212.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Has the
department advertised for artisans?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What classification?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
This is
the advertisement:
Recruits
Skilled Tradesmen for R.C.A.F.
Vacancies exist in the Royal Canadian Air Force for skilled men in the following trades:-
Acetylene welder, armament artificer, air rigger, clerk, aero engine fitter, machinist, motor boat crewman, motor mechanic, photographer, sheet metal worker, storekeeper, tailor, instrument maker and wireless operator.
Applicants must be British subjects, between the age of 18 and 31 years, unmarried, medically fit (subject to examination) and willing to enlist for a period of five years. Good prospects, pay dependent upon proficiency. Quarters, food and uniform provided. Any expenses incurred before enlistment must be borne by applicant.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
What is the proportion of successful applicants to the total number?

Supply-National Defence

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
The
applications are receivable in the districts. We have not the record here, but there are thousands.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: We are limited not by the type of applicant but by facilities to take care of applications?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: At the Edmonton air school in 1929 there was quite a discussion about how to train pilots. A certain amount of civil work was done by the Edmonton instructors and we had local schools at Cam-rose and other places. Is a grant given under this or some other item to encourage these young men in flying? I was a member of an air club at Vegreville and took the ground school course, but the fees are high-$100 for the course and $10 an hour for flying time. We have been doing that work voluntarily.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: My hon. friend is referring to the flying clubs. They used to be under the jurisdiction of the defence department, but for the past three years they have been under the Department of Transport. The vote for training pilots is the only item in the estimates under which there will be cooperation; otherwise it is under the Department of Transport.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What coordination is there between the two departments in the training of pilots? Does the Department of Transport train its own pilots?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: The pilots trained by the Department of National Defence are not transferred to the Department of Transport?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: No. If there were an emergency the pilots trained by the other department would be of great value.

Item agreed to.
Air services.
200. Buildings and works-chargeable to ordinary account, $111,000.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What was the cost of the Spencer home which was acquired by the air force in Vancouver?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: The matter was heard several months ago but the judgment of the exchequer court has not yet come down.

Item agreed to.
Air services.
201. Chargeable to capital account, $4,212,000.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What is this item for?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: If you refer to civil government air operations; this is to provide for expenses incident to air operations undertaken by the Royal Canadian Air Force for the topographical and air survey bureau. A committee was appointed on air service and it makes recommendations as to the requirements of other departments.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Is this work increasing in volume? I understand that there is a feeling among the private air companies that a good deal of this work should be done by them. They think that it would help them to maintain our air services in the northern part of Canada and that the department should not be doing this work but should be training its men for fighting purposes rather than in civilian aviation.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Topography is one of the most valuable parts of the training a pilot receives, and in addition to that, the requirements of other departments of government from the point of view of national development are quite numerous. In my opinion the air force is rendering an invaluable service. It is national work of a high order.

Item agreed to.
Air services.
204. Chargeable to ordinary account, $2,771,840.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: How many Canadian pilots are to be trained each year?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: In addition to the number provided for in the ordinary estimates, there will be a total of 126 under the specific vote.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Fifty British and 76 Canadian.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: The same number each year?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Unless we decide to increase the number. Our requirements in pilots will be between 500 and 600 when our final complement is established.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Under this item, chargeable to ordinary account, has anything been done by the government, as I asked early this session many times, for the protection of the civilian population in case of emergency? Has any study, or survey, or register, been made of that matter before it is too late for it?

42%
Supply-National Defence

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
That
question was taken up the other day by a neighbour of the hon. member, and I explained that a committee has been functioning on that very point for the last twelve months at least, and certain plans have been drawn up.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What proportion of the cost of this pilot training scheme is to be paid by Great Britain?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: That has not been definitely decided; the matter is subject to adjustment. The suggestion is that the per capita cost to the British government will be the same as to the Canadian government. That would be refunded to the consolidated revenue fund.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What provision have we in Canada for training pilots for the very fast planes? The minister knows that there was a crash in Vancouver a few weeks ago of a Hawker Hurricane plane; presumably the pilots have not been given a chance to get thorough training in flying these very fast machines.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: The difficulty in the past, as my hon. friend knows, is that we did not have a sufficient number of advanced or intermediate training machines. As a matter of fact since this occurrence I have seen the pilot who had the crash flying magnificently. We have no worry about the pilots. We have had, in the past, about the machines, but I am glad to say that within the next few weeks we shall have some forty-five planes of that type, so that that difficulty will not occur again.

Item agreed to.
Air services.
205. Chargeable to capital account (equipments and properties) (commitments $761,840), $3,228,160.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: What are the commitments in this item?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Training of pilots, capital account, for these advanced trainers, single engine, commitment, $441,840-not those coming immediately but those that cannot be obtained this year. Then, aircraft spares, commitment, $200,000. In connection with buildings such as construction of new roadway, heating and steam distribution, stores and electrical and telephone connections, et cetera, $120,000.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
There is a question I wanted to ask under a previous item. A good many Canadians took advantage of the short service course in the Royal Air Force. The
[Mr. Church.)
term is coming to an end and I know some are most anxious to transfer, if one can use that term, into the Royal Canadian Air Force. Are there any facilities open to those young men?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I think that suggestion is very much worth while, and I shall be glad to look into it.

Item agreed to.
Militia services.
621. Engineer services and works: capital account, $145,000.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Will the minister explain
this item?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
This is required in connection with the defences of the port of Saint John, New Brunswick. It provides for the construction of certain gun emplacements there. They will be of a semipermanent nature, constructed of concrete, with surface magazines. The amount also covers cost of acquiring site, clearing the area and construction of roads and communications.
Further down there is an item of $73,625 in connection with guns for the proposed fortifications. Also general stores, $100,000; clothing, armament and signal equipment-that is for boots for the non-permanent active militia. For a survey of the situation with reference to the possibility of various arsenals and shops for gun production, $20,000. Then, ammunition procurement and general stores, including dominion arsenals, capital account, $203,375, of which $151,375 is for coast defence ammunition. That also is for Saint John. There is $52,000 for Lindsay arsenal and $100,000 for the increased training for the non-permanent active militia, of which $65,000 is for actual training and $35,000 for clerical help and assistance. Then naval engineering: $300,000 for the construction of oil tanks on Vancouver island. For the defence purchasing board, $75,000.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: How long does the minister anticipate it will take to erect the fortifications at Saint John? And is this $145,000 the full amount?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
No, I
gave two or three amounts; I will give them again. An amount of $145,000 for engineering services and works provides for the construction of certain gun emplacements. The sum of $53,625 is for purchase of certain artillery for the emplacement at Saint John and $151,000 is for the purchase of ammunition for the gun proposed to be obtained.

Supply-National Defence

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I understand it takes three years to develop these fortifications; is this for the first year or the three years?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: The guns will be there inside of two or three months- a few months.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Do they not require the fortifications before they have the gun?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: This is a semi-permanent fortification, so that we can get at least interim armament there as soon as possible.

Item agreed to.
Militia services.
622. Ordinary account, $100,000.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Does this provide boots for the whole non-permanent militia?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I think this provides for 30,000 pairs. Of course we have a stock already that we use only for the permanent force and reserve, and we can get some more next year. I think this will provide all that will be required.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: Then the whole militia will not be provided with boots this year?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Yes, I
think if we draw on the supplies we now have we shall be able to meet all requirements.

Item agreed to.
Militia services.
626. Capital account, $73,625.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I see there is an amount of $20,000 for preliminary expenses, including surveys and preparation of plans towards obtaining Canadian-made guns. Is that the amount provided in clause 1 of the Bren gun contract for preliminary expenses?

speechtext:
In his speech of April 26 the minister mentioned that purchases were being made of 14 anti-aircraft guns of 4-5 calibre, and 4 of 3-inch calibre, at a total cost of $1,289,240, and that munitions had been ordered to the value of $553,140. The war office announced last night that no further orders are to be given for the 4'5-inch anti-aircraft gun after the initial contracts have been completed.
Tests in the last few days with a 3-7 on a fixed base have shown that it is equal to and even better than the 4-5 gun in performance. It has an equal range but a more rapid rate of fire.

speechtext: Will the minister give some details as to the $20,000 item for preliminary expenses, including surveys and preparation of plans towards obtaining Canadian made guns?

be an expenditure to make a thorough and specialized report in regard to other government buildings, the cost of manufacture in government buildings or railway shops, and matters of the kind, so that we shall have a complete and up to date report with reference to the possibility of producing guns in Canada.

speechtext:
Will the
amount be paid to government officers, to an engineering company, or to whom?

On account of the shortening of the hours of civilian firemen there was an actual reduction of $40,000 in training expenditures. This additional amount will eliminate the dissatisfaction, and in addition will give clerical assistance.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext:
Surely this is not a very
large matter. It would not take as much to transport those soldiers as to carry a dozen delegates to the league. Surely there should be a larger vote for transport and travelling of the non-permanent active militia.

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I wish to draw attention to an important lache, if I may so describe it. We have pictures in the lobbies and spread throughout the House of Commons. maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE
speechtext: I hope my hon. friend is not attributing that atrocity to the Minister of National Defence, because it is not under my jurisdiction. I believe such matters come under the Department of the Secretary of State.

speechtext: I have brought to the attention of the government the activities of Japanese interests on the British Columbia coast. In fact, Japanese interests directly related to Tokyo are acquiring important timber lands and mineral claims and even at some points are excavating for purpose of building storage tunnels. A return tabled to the house indicates that the Department of National Defence has no information. Would the minister make a statement as to whether or not steps have been taken by officials of his department to see that strategic sites are not left in the hands of potential enemies?

maintopic: STATEMENT IN DEBATE ON DEFENCE ESTIMATES RESPECTING ROYAL MILITARY COLLEGE

speechtext: Hon. IAN MACKENZIE (Minister of National Defence) moved the second reading of and concurrence in amendments made by the senate to Bill No. 38, to establish a defence purchasing board.

maintopic: NATIONAL DEFENCE
subtopic: CREATION OP DEFENCE PURCHASING BOARD-CONCURRENCE IN SENATE AMENDMENTS
speechtext: There was one amendment to the effect that the chairman shall be ex officio a member of the defence council.

maintopic: NATIONAL DEFENCE
subtopic: CREATION OP DEFENCE PURCHASING BOARD-CONCURRENCE IN SENATE AMENDMENTS
speechtext: The hon. member brought this amendment to my attention. I took it up with the deputy minister of justice and he believes that because the defence council is mentioned in a former statute, this amendment is quite in order.

maintopic: NATIONAL DEFENCE
subtopic: CREATION OP DEFENCE PURCHASING BOARD-CONCURRENCE IN SENATE AMENDMENTS
speechtext: Is that the only amendment?

maintopic: NATIONAL DEFENCE

speechtext:
There are two or three minor ones. Perhaps I had better run through them. The amendment to which I have just referred substitutes the words "he shall be, ex officio, a member of the defence council of the Department of National
Defence" for the words "or a shareholder of any corporation or company manufacturing guns, cannon, small arms, munitions, naval ships, military aircraft or other equipment or supplies used exclusively or primarily for war purposes." Then on page 2, line 46, for the words "two other members" substitute the words "one other member." Then a new subsection is inserted in section 7, as follows:
The board shall also have the exclusive power to superintend and enforce the performance of all contracts within the meaning of section two of this act, including such thereof as shall have been already negotiated, executed or partly performed at the time when this act comes into force, according to the respective terms of such contracts, and not otherwise, but subject to variance of such terms by mutual consent in the same manner as if the variance were a contract negotiated after this act comes into force.
This amendment gives the board jurisdiction to deal with existing contracts. Then in section 6 the words "under this part or already negotiated, executed or partly performed at the time when this act comes into force" are substituted for the words "pursuant to the provisions of this part." Then a new paragraph (c) is added to section 7, subsection 3, as follows:
In the determination of net profit, the board shall apply the principles and practices as to accounting and otherwise governing the determination of taxable income under the Income War Tax Act.
In subsection 9 of section 7, for the words "and (b)" substitute the words "or (b) contracts or subcontracts already entered into at the time when this act comes into force, or (c)." The rest are minor amendments.

maintopic: NATIONAL DEFENCE
subtopic: CREATION OP DEFENCE PURCHASING BOARD-CONCURRENCE IN SENATE AMENDMENTS

In regard
